title: Visualizing and exploring genomic information for non-protein-coding RNA identification using ApolloRNA
protocol: In the directory 'My Documents', create the subdirectory 'Applications'.
In the directory 'Applications', create the subdirectory 'Apollo'.
Access the download Apollo page at "http://www.fruitfly.org/annot/apollo/install.html".
In the line 'Windows', in the column 'includes Java VM', right-click the link 'Download' and save the file in the directory 'Apollo'.
Double-click the downloaded file 'install.exe' and follow instructions choosing the 'Apollo' directory as installation directory.
Create the directory '~/Applications'.
In the directory 'Applications', create the subdirectory 'Apollo'.
Access the download Apollo page at "http://www.fruitfly.org/annot/apollo/install.html".
In the line 'Linux', in the column 'includes Java VM', right-click the link 'Download' and save the file in the directory 'Apollo'.
Open a terminal window.
Move to the directory 'Apollo'.
Type: sh ./apolloinst.bin and follow instructions choosing 'Apollo' for installation directory.
Configure Apollo for Java.
Open a terminal window, move to the directory 'Apollo' and type: **pwd**.
Add a line defining the JavaPath variable as the Apollo path extended with '/jre' in the file 'apollo.cfg'.
Create the subdirectory 'Applications/Apollo' if it doesn't exist.
Access the download Apollo page at "http://www.fruitfly.org/annot/apollo/install.html".
In the line 'Mac OS X', right-click the link 'Download' and save the file in the directory 'Apollo'.
Double-click the downloaded file 'install', and follow instructions choosing the 'Apollo' directory as installation directory.
Open a terminal window and type: **java -version**.
Download and install GhostScript using option A or B depending on the operating system.
Access the download GhostScript page at "http://www.ghostscript.com/awki".
Right-click the link 'gs856w32.exe' for Windows installation, then click 'Save link as...' and save the file in the directory 'Applications'.
Double-click the downloaded file 'gs856w32.exe' and follow the instructions.
Open a terminal window for Linux or MAC installation and type: gs -h.
Right-click the link 'ghostscript-8.56.tar.gz' then click 'Save link as...' to save in directory 'Applications'.
Move to the directory 'Applications' and type: tar xzvf ghostscript-8.56.tar.gz, cd ghostscript-8.56.
Rename 'apollo.jar' to 'apollo.jar.save' in the directory 'Apollo'.
Download 'apollo.jar' from "http://mulcyber.toulouse.inra.fr/gf/project/apollorna/frs/" and save it in the directory 'Apollo'.
Access ftp NCBI page at "ftp://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/genomes/Bacteria/Pyrococcus_abyssi".
Copy the text of 'NC_000868.gbk' from the accessed link.
Paste the copied GenBank data into the ApolloRNA convert data page at "http://carlit.toulouse.inra.fr/ApolloRNA/convert.html".
Select 'Genbank' in the 'Input format' list and 'Game XML' in the 'Output format' list, then click the 'Convert' button.
Copy the resulting text and paste it into a new file called 'NC_000868.xml'.
Access the TransTermHP page at "http://transterm.cbcb.umd.edu/cgi-bin/transterm/predictions.pl".
Click 'Pyrococcus abyssi GE5'.
Copy all displaying text starting with the line: SEQUENCE gi|10954552|ref|NC_001773.1|.
Paste the copied data into ApolloRNA convert data page.
In the 'Input format' list, select 'TransTermHP'.
In the 'Output format' list, select 'Game XML'.
Enter 1 for the beginning and 1765118 for the end in the related genomic sequence coordinates fields.
Click the 'Convert' button.
Copy the resulting text and paste it into a new file called 'NC_000868_TransTermHP.xml'.
Launch Apollo using option A or B depending on the operating system.
For Windows: Click the Apollo icon in the directory 'Apollo'.
For Linux or MAC: Open a terminal window, move to the directory 'Apollo' and type: bin/Apollo.
Choose 'GAME XML format' in the list 'Choose data source'.
Click the 'Browse...' button and select the file 'NC_000868.xml'.
Click the 'Open' button after selecting the file.
In the Apollo load data window, click the 'Ok' button.
Open the 'File' menu and click the 'Layer more results or annotations...' item.
Choose 'GAME XML format' in the list 'Choose data source'.
Click the 'Browse...' button again.
Select the file 'NC_000868_TransTermHP.xml'.
Click the 'Open' button after selecting the file.
In the Apollo load data window, click the 'Ok' button.
Click twice on the 'X10' zoom button in the main Apollo window.
Click the inorganic polyphosphate/ATP-NAD kinase protein annotation to display more information.
Open the 'Edit' menu and click the 'Find...' item.
Type 'PABt04' in the field 'Name'.
Click the 'Find' button on the line.
Click the 'X.1' zoom button to change scale.
Open the 'RNA' menu and click the 'Secondary structure compute...' item.
Click the 'Close' button after the secondary structure computation window opens.
Type 'PABsnRNA29' in the 'Find' window and click the 'Find' button.
Select subsequence from 1403702 to 1403711 on the sno C/D RNA called 'PABsnRNA29'.
Open the 'RNA' menu and click the 'Search RNA/RNA interaction' item.
Type genomic positions 205039 to 206541 in the top part of the window, and choose strand +.
Click the 'Search' button to launch the search for targets in the specified regions.
Click the first interaction picture in the new window to visualize the interaction.
Close the visualization window.
Go to the ApolloRNA page "http://carlit.toulouse.inra.fr/ApolloRNA/apollornauserguide.html".
Click the link 'NC_000868_mfe150.txt' and save the file on your computer.
Open the 'Analysis' menu and click the 'Show quantitative variable...' item.
In the first table of the window, in the first line, click the 'Load...' button.
Select the file 'NC_000868_mfe150.txt' and click the 'Open' button.
In the column 'Color', click the black rectangle, choose the red color, and click the 'OK' button.
In the second table of the window, in the third line 'ComputeGC%', click the 'Show' checkbox.
In the column 'Color', click the black rectangle and choose the blue color.
Click the 'OK' button and then click the 'Close' button.
In the yet opened 'Find' window, in the field 'Name', type **16S**.
Click the 'Find' button on the line.
Click the 'X.1' zoom button to change scale.
Move down the superior vertical scrollbar to see RNA annotations on the direct strand.
